description: The line plot illustrates the performance of knowledge probing after applying different editing methods to LLMs, with accuracy measured in percentage (ACC) on the y-axis and co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale (ranging from 1 to 1000) on the x-axis. The "Base" method, representing the LLM without editing, shows a steady increase in accuracy from approximately 63% to 69% as the co-occurrence number increases. The "MEND" method starts at around 69% and rises to about 77%, while "FT" begins at roughly 64% and reaches approximately 71%. "MEMIT" starts at about 68% and increases to around 75%, and "ROME" begins at approximately 73% and climbs to about 81%. All methods exhibit a positive trend in accuracy with increasing co-occurrence number, with "ROME" consistently achieving the highest accuracy across the range, followed by "MEND," "MEMIT," "FT," and "Base."
